about: Verses whose length is far from the median of the other translations for a known reason, reviewed by reading each one (Oct 29 2026). scripts/test-bible-integrity.mts fails on any outlier NOT listed here, which is how a cut-short verse like NCV Numbers 7 (17 of 89 verses) is caught even when every verse number is present. Key: translation, book, chapter:first verse of the entry.
rule: SHORT: fewer than 0.4 x the median word count of the other translations over the same verses, when that median is at least 10 words. LONG: more than 2.6 x the median and more than 15 words above it.

groups.reason: A list printed one or two names or places per verse (genealogies, city lists), so each verse is a few words while other translations write full sentences
NLT prints the census in Numbers 1-2 as a table: one 'Tribe - number' row per pair of verses
Thought-for-thought wording moves words between neighbouring verses; the chapter as a whole is complete
NCV prints the twelve identical offerings of Numbers 7:12-83 once, as one combined passage
Words found in some ancient manuscripts that this translation includes (Dead Sea Scrolls, Septuagint, Textus Receptus)
The NIV prints a bracketed note about John 7:53-8:11 in its text, before verse 53
CSB numbers the closing blessing as 2 Corinthians 13:13 (others: 13:14)
